decision: Open with the problem in the users' words before any solution
why: Architecture choices only make sense against the problem they answer.
value: Reviewers judge the fit of each decision.

decision: Ownership is split across Frontend, Backend, Data and AI
why: A founding engineer is hired for range; the split shows it without adjectives.
value: Depth in each layer is visible and checkable.

decision: Outcomes are labelled as measured on the real systems the fictitious case models
why: The products are fictitious; the engineering outcomes are not, and the difference must be explicit.
alternative: Attribute metrics to the fictitious company.

decision: The gallery includes the AI surfaces, each linking to its live trace or approval flow
why: AI claims should be inspected in context, not described.
alternative: Describe the AI features in text.
value: Every AI surface is one click from its evidence.
